chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: Mildred Bailey's warning and Midge Williams
summary: Mildred Bailey advised her on style so she wouldn't be a second Ella; Midge Williams was more commercial.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: You know, I remember very vividly when I first came to New York, Mildred Bailey was popular. And she was among the musicians, you know, that used to come in because she was probably with Kurby and Buster and Red, you know, they were all together. And I had the audacity to approach Mildred Bailey and here I am, you know, just coming out of left field, but I said to Mildred Bailey I told her, I said, 'I think you're being too much influenced by Billie Holiday.' I don't think it made her very happy and I shouldn't have said that but I didn't know any better at the time. And of course when I was singing around Homestead, you know, in the little after-the-ballgame's spots, they were calling me the little Mildred Bailey, you know. So you imitate. You do do what you can. In fact, as I said before, when I first came to New York I was imitating ever so much that they had to get me onto 'Loch Lomont' and things

like that because I would have been a second Ella Fitzgerald.
Yeah, and the fact even you mentioned before Midge Williams.
She had something of an Ella Fitzgerald style.
No Midge was, I think Midge was more commercial, which I became when I got associated with "Loch Loman".
Well I've only heard two or three things by her on jazz anthologies.
Well, I listened to her on this recording. I think she's on this album, the Frankie Newton album, isn't she? Something reissued recently.
That's right, she is on that album.
Yeah, and I hadn't remembered too much of Midge Williams style in those early days. I don't think she was considered a stylists. She was

I think this had to do with her accompaniment, being on this album with Frankie Newton group, sort of gave her sort of a lift she probably didn't have in the studios she was working with, studio musicians. And even the records she made were probably studio musicians.
